healthcareSystem: Government-run healthcare with limited capacity. Vaiola Hospital in Nuku'alofa is the main facility. Outer islands have basic health clinics only.
qualityNotes: Basic healthcare available in Nuku'alofa. Vaiola Hospital handles most cases but lacks specialist services. Outer islands have very limited medical facilities. Serious conditions require evacuation to New Zealand or Australia.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open 8:30am-4:30pm weekdays, limited Saturday hours. Very few options outside Nuku'alofa.
pharmacyTips: The hospital pharmacy and a few private pharmacies in Nuku'alofa stock basic medications. Bring all needed medications with you. Stock is unreliable and limited.
prescriptionRules: Prescription required for most medications. Limited availability even with a prescription. English spoken widely — communication is straightforward.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter and keep in original packaging.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter for all prescription medications. Keep medications in original packaging. English documentation is fine. Bring a full supply of all medications — do not rely on local availability.

travelInsurance.tips: Medical evacuation insurance is ESSENTIAL. Evacuation to New Zealand can cost $25,000-60,000+. Ensure your policy covers remote island evacuation, diving, and cyclone-related emergencies.

vaccinations.notes: No special vaccinations required for most travelers. Dengue fever is present — use insect repellent. Zika virus has been reported. No malaria in Tonga.

waterNotes: Tap water in Nuku'alofa is generally treated but may not meet Western standards. Bottled water is recommended, especially on outer islands. After cyclones, water quality deteriorates significantly.
foodSafetyTips: Food at hotels and established restaurants is generally safe. Be cautious with raw seafood from informal vendors. Fresh tropical fruit is widely available. Wash produce with bottled water on outer islands.
medicalTourismNote: Tonga is not a medical tourism destination. Tongans needing specialist care travel to New Zealand or Australia.
sources: New Zealand Ministry of Health — Pacific Health
metaDescription: Health guide for traveling to Tonga. Emergency numbers, Vaiola Hospital info, water safety, vaccinations, and medical evacuation to New Zealand.

dentalCare.availability: Basic dental services at Vaiola Hospital. Very limited private options.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care is very basic. Bring any dental supplies you may need. No cosmetic dentistry available.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Go to Vaiola Hospital dental clinic for emergencies. Limited hours — weekdays only.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: No dedicated crisis line. Contact Vaiola Hospital: +676-23-200
mentalHealth.internationalLine: Crisis Text Line: text HOME to 741741 (US-based, available globally via SMS)
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very limited. No private mental health practices for tourists.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are extremely limited in Tonga. If you need ongoing support, consider telehealth options before traveling.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is very limited throughout Tonga.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Vaiola Hospital has basic wheelchair access but is not fully accessible.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Roads can be rough and unpaved on outer islands.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Bring all mobility aids and supplies. Terrain can be challenging. Contact your accommodation in advance about accessibility.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mask mandates. Masks may be requested in healthcare facilities.
covidStatus.testing: Limited COVID testing available at Vaiola Hospital.
covidStatus.notes: COVID services are minimal. Bring rapid tests if concerned.

insuranceClaimProcess: Most facilities require upfront cash payment. Obtain itemized receipts with diagnosis codes. Submit claims to your insurer after returning home. Credit cards are not widely accepted at government facilities.

commonCosts.note: Costs shown in USD equivalents. Government hospital fees are low but service is basic. Private clinics charge more.

medicalEvacuation.note: Evacuation from outer islands requires boat/small plane to Tongatapu first, then air evacuation to New Zealand. Delays are common due to weather and limited flights.
